g0.rationale: §2.2 five-step test. Step 1: authoritative directions located (aggregated, moderate confidence). Step 2: the directions label the modes themselves — 'Als Haarmaske: auf das nasse Haar auftragen, 3 Minuten einwirken lassen und gründlich ausspülen' has a stated contact time and a rinse and qualifies; 'Als Leave-in-Pflege … nicht ausspülen' fails the rinse conjunct; 'Auch als Over-Night-Pflege verwendbar' is leave-on and falls under the charter's overnight exclusion for that mode. Step 3: exactly one mode qualifies → mode-scoped classification. Charter F1 names Balea Aqua Hyaluron 3 in 1 as a live boundary case that is eligible mode-scoped.

tailMarker.anomalyNote: No §3.1 anomaly. The marker at 9 in a 15-entry list demotes Isoamyl Laurate @10, Behentrimonium Chloride @11 and Cetrimonium Chloride @12 — so this formula's second and third cationic species are both non-contributing, and the credited segment is humectant-led rather than cationic-led. DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE (rank 4) — the only cationic species above the tail
BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (11) and CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (12) — two further cationics, both BELOW tail_index 9

conditioningLevel.derivation: S1 = NOT satisfied (one cationic above the tail; the other two are demoted). S2 = satisfied (Cetearyl Alcohol @2). S3 = NOT satisfied (one lipid above the tail). Count = 1 of 3.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moderate`: §9.1's 'everything else, including exactly one satisfied signal'.

`high` does not apply: only S2 holds. Had the marker fallen two ranks later, S1 would have been satisfied by the Behentrimonium/Cetrimonium pair and the value would have moved to `high` — recorded as a sensitivity, not as a reason to move it.
`low` does not apply: Cetearyl Alcohol @2 defeats its second conjunct, and there is a lipid above the tail.
Confidence `moderate` by §9.1's rule: high confidence requires ≥2 signals pointing the same way.
counterSignals: Two of the formula's three cationic species are in the tail. Under the lexicon §0.2 boundary-band caution, Isoamyl Laurate @10 and Behentrimonium Chloride @11 sit within two ranks of the marker; per this lane's policy that caps confidence and does not move the value.
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support.

primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: one M1 base observation, one M5 cluster observation — disjoint per §6 rule 3. Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5, no bond); `curl_support` blocked (single cationic, no polymer, no high-slip breadth); `color_care` blocked (no candidate, no positioning); `lightness` blocked (weight `moderate`, not `low`). Step 4: the D5 guard is applied and clears on all four criteria.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moisture`: D5 guard criterion 1 (≥3 distinct humectants above the tail with ≥2 non-glycerin) is met with four and three; criterion 2 (not the baseline) is met unusually cleanly, because there is no rich R1/R4 architecture here at all — one esterquat and one plant oil — so the cluster cannot be an M1 product in M5 clothing; criterion 3 (no richer special-purpose route wins) is met because every step-3 route was blocked; criterion 4 (hydrolyzed proteins not counted) is vacuous, there are none.
`general` does not apply: a candidate cleared its threshold at step 4.
`smoothing` does not apply: reached only at step 6, and there is no silicone, no substantive polymer and one lipid — the architecture does not extend beyond the ordinary mask base.
`shine` does not apply: §9.5.4 criterion 1 fails outright (no alignment-oriented R2/R3 route above the tail), so the 'glänzendes Haar' claim never reaches criterion 3.

Confidence `high` is earned under §9.5.3's own confidence rule: ≥3 distinct qualifying humectants above the tail with at least one within the first five ranks (Glycerin @3, Panthenol @5), a resolved tail marker, and no competing route. This is the only `high`-confidence focus in the cohort.

Discrimination check against the ruled anchor set: D5 was tested on four real formulas, and this product is one of the two the ruling says should CLEAR. It clears, on the same evidence the ruling cited (four humectants above the tail, no protein/bond/silicone routes).
counterSignals: Aloe is reconstituted powder ('Leaf Juice Powder' in the source list) at unquantifiable level; counted once, never strong. Excluding it entirely still leaves three members with two non-glycerin, so the guard clears either way.
No glycol appears in the cluster, so lexicon family 7's solvent-role discount is not engaged at all — unusual, and it makes this the cleanest cluster in the cohort.
limitations: Wording rule observed absolutely (D5, binding): never 'hydrates', 'proven hydration', 'moisturizes', or 'restores moisture balance'. The humectant evidence base is weak at the hair-fibre outcome level (lexicon W1) and this value is a comparative architecture signal only.
'Hygral fatigue' is an unestablished construct and appears nowhere in this record.

blindToFinalChanges.reason: Unblinding changed nothing. The moisture focus was determined blind from the cluster; the hydration positioning only corroborated it, and §11 step 4 does not list the moisture guard as a channel claims may influence in any case. The 'glänzendes Haar' claim was refused because §9.5.4 criterion 1 failed before criterion 3 was reachable. No dual tie, no bond claim, no lightness positioning, no colour positioning.

adjudicationPoints.title: The D5 moisture guard reproduces its ruled anchor exactly — report as a passed check
adjudicationPoints.body: D5's guard was ruled after testing on four real formulas, with this product named as one of the two that should clear ('Balea Aqua Hyaluron 3in1: 4 humectants above tail, no protein/bond/silicone routes'). Running the operationalized §9.5.3 criteria against the frozen INCI reproduces that outcome on the same evidence, at high confidence, with the cluster surviving even if Aloe is discounted entirely. The guard's discriminating power on THIS product is not in doubt. Where the guard is fragile is at the other end — on rich masks where cheap cluster members (glycerin, betaine, panthenol) coexist with a heavy lipid stack, and criterion 2 has to carry the whole load with no operational test. See AP-10-CRITERION2.

adjudicationPoints.title: A product with a stated overnight leave-on mode is eligible mode-scoped, while a product whose ONLY mode is overnight is excluded
adjudicationPoints.body: The charter excludes 'leave-on-only masks and overnight treatments' and names Bali Curls Bonding Repair Overnight Elixir as excluded. This product states an Over-Night-Pflege mode too, and is eligible — correctly, because F1 scopes classification to the qualifying rinse-out mode and the overnight mode is simply uncovered. The rule is coherent, but the charter's exclusion bullet reads as a product-level exclusion while F1 makes it a mode-level one. Worth a one-line clarification so a reviewer does not exclude a 3in1 on seeing an overnight mode.
